home-remodeling.h1: Whole-home remodeling in the Village Beautiful
home-remodeling.hero_sub: PGX Builders Group takes Miami Shores houses down to the good bones and rebuilds them: permitted through the Village, engineered to South Florida code, and supervised daily by a licensed general contractor, CGC1539072.
home-remodeling.local_heading: A village that knows what it looks like
intro_paragraphs: Miami Shores was laid out in the 1920s by the Shoreland Company as America's Mediterranean, and the housing stock still shows it: barrel-tile Mediterranean Revival homes near Grand Concourse and NE 96th Street, 1930s and 1940s houses on the numbered streets, and postwar ranches filling in toward the Country Club. Owners here rarely want a teardown. They want the arches, the casement proportions, and the street presence kept, and the original floor plan, wiring, and plumbing completely rethought. That is the home remodeling we do most in the Village.

Permits run through the Miami Shores Village Building Department, and the Village looks harder at appearances than most jurisdictions. Its code requires buildings to stay harmonious with the neighborhood in character, appearance, and even exterior color, with the Planning and Zoning Board weighing in on work that does not fit. Dozens of homes carry Village historic designation, which adds Historic Preservation Board review. Windows and doors go in impact-rated, carrying the Miami-Dade product approvals the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone demands. We assemble those packages ourselves and present work the reviewers can approve the first time.

PGX has been remodeling South Florida houses for more than 20 years, over 150 projects of it, every one permitted and inspected. In Miami Shores that means a fixed written scope before demolition starts, a supervisor on your site every day, floors and finish work protected while the trades move through, and one accountable team from the first estimate to the warranty call. A remodel is a promise. We keep it in writing.

faqs.q: Do I need Village approval before remodeling a Miami Shores home?
faqs.a: Every remodel needs permits from the Miami Shores Village Building Department. Interior work generally stays between you and the plan reviewers, but exterior changes are held to the Village's harmony standards for character, appearance, and color, and can go to the Planning and Zoning Board if they do not fit the neighborhood. If your home carries a Village historic designation, the Historic Preservation Board reviews changes too. We map the approval path before we price the work.

faqs.q: How long does permitting take in Miami Shores Village?
faqs.a: The Village quotes 15 business days to review most residential remodel and addition applications for completeness, and full approval depends on how many disciplines review the plans and how quickly revisions turn around. Clean, coordinated drawings are the real schedule tool, which is why we submit complete packages covering architectural, structural, and MEP work rather than testing the reviewers' patience one correction at a time.

faqs.q: Can you modernize a Mediterranean Revival house without ruining it?
faqs.a: That is most of our work in the Shores. The envelope, meaning the arches, barrel tile, stucco, and casement proportions, is what the Village and the street value, so we keep it and rebuild what is behind it: layout, electrical, plumbing, air conditioning, insulation, openings. Done right, the house reads original from the sidewalk and functions like new construction inside. That is why the design phase matters as much as the build.

faqs.q: What kind of budget does a Miami Shores remodel call for?
faqs.a: It depends on scope more than square footage. A cosmetic refresh and a full-gut with structural openings are entirely different projects. We are a high-end contractor, so we will not be the cheapest bid; we will be the one with a fixed written scope, engineering done properly, and no surprise change orders manufactured mid-project. After a walk-through we give you a real number tied to a real scope, and we hold to it.

faqs.q: Who pulls the permits and handles inspections?
faqs.a: We do. PGX Builders Group is a licensed and insured Florida general contractor, license CGC1539072. We pull permits under our license, schedule every inspection, and meet the inspector on site. You should never be asked to pull an owner-builder permit for a contractor's work, in the Shores or anywhere else. If a contractor suggests it, that tells you what you need to know.

kitchen-remodeling.title: Miami Shores Kitchen Remodeling, Done Right | PGX Builders
kitchen-remodeling.meta_description: Kitchen remodeling in Miami Shores: custom cabinetry, stone counters, and opened-up layouts for the Village's older homes. Licensed and permitted. (786) 273-2524.
kitchen-remodeling.hero_sub: Custom cabinetry, stone counters, and opened-up layouts for Miami Shores kitchens, designed around how you cook, permitted through the Village Building Department, and supervised daily by our licensed team.
kitchen-remodeling.local_heading: The hardest-working room in an old house
intro_paragraphs: The Shoreland Company drew Miami Shores in the 1920s, when a kitchen was a working room hidden behind a swinging door, and plenty of houses near Grand Concourse and the streets east of NE 2nd Avenue still cook that way. The postwar ranches closer to the Country Club traded the swinging door for a narrow galley. Owners of high-end homes in the Village want the same three things from us: a real island, storage that fits how they actually cook, and a kitchen that finally faces the family instead of the wall.

A kitchen remodel here is permitted through the Miami Shores Village Building Department, with electrical, plumbing, and mechanical trades each inspected. Removing the wall between kitchen and dining room is structural work in a masonry house, so we bring the engineering, not optimism. If your project touches the exterior, say a new window over the sink or a relocated door to the terrace, the Village's harmony standards apply and any new opening needs a Miami-Dade product approval for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. We fold all of it into one permit package.

PGX Builders Group builds kitchens the way high-end clients expect them built: cabinetry measured against walls that stopped being square decades ago, stone templated after the boxes are set, appliances relocated with the panel capacity to actually run them. You get a fixed written scope before demolition, dust containment that genuinely contains, and a supervisor on site every day. After 20-plus years and more than 150 remodels across South Florida, we have learned the kitchen is where trust is won or lost. We plan accordingly.

faqs.q: Does a kitchen remodel in Miami Shores require a permit?
faqs.a: Yes. Cabinet-for-cabinet swaps with no trade work are the rare exception; the moment plumbing moves, circuits are added, or walls open, you need permits from the Miami Shores Village Building Department with inspections for each trade. Unpermitted kitchen work surfaces at appraisal or sale, and retroactive permitting costs more than doing it right. We permit everything, which is one reason our projects close cleanly.

faqs.q: Can we remove the wall between the kitchen and dining room?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Most walls in the Village's masonry houses can come out once an engineer sizes the beam that replaces them. We handle the structural drawings, the permit, and the shoring, and we will tell you plainly if a wall is doing too much work to remove economically. What we will not do is take out a bearing wall on a hunch.

faqs.q: Will adding a window over the sink trigger Village review?
faqs.a: It can. A new or enlarged opening changes the exterior, which brings in the Village's harmony standards for character and appearance, and the window itself must be an impact-rated unit with a Miami-Dade product approval for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone. None of this is a reason to skip the window; morning light over a sink is worth paperwork. It is a reason to have a contractor who files it correctly.

faqs.q: How long does a full kitchen remodel take?
faqs.a: Plan in two phases. Custom cabinetry and stone carry real lead times, often a couple of months before anything is demolished, and construction itself typically runs several weeks to a few months depending on structural work and appliance relocations. We schedule demolition only when materials are secured, because a kitchen torn out while cabinets sit in a factory queue is how remodels earn their bad reputation.

faqs.q: What should we budget for a high-end kitchen in Miami Shores?
faqs.a: Custom cabinetry, natural stone, and layout changes put a serious kitchen well into six figures in many cases, and we would rather say that plainly than surprise you later. Where the money goes is your call; cabinetry and stone drive cost more than appliances do. We build a fixed written scope around your priorities so the number is real before demolition, not discovered after it.

kitchen-remodeling.cta_sub: Bring your wish list and your least favorite cabinet. We will measure, talk layout honestly, and write you a fixed scope — in English o en español.

bathroom-remodeling.title: Bathroom Remodeling for Miami Shores, FL Homes | PGX Builders
bathroom-remodeling.meta_description: Bathroom remodeling in Miami Shores, FL. Primary suites, marble showers, and waterproofing done right in homes from the 1920s on. PGX Builders, (786) 273-2524.
bathroom-remodeling.h1: New bathrooms for old Miami Shores houses
bathroom-remodeling.hero_sub: Primary suites, frameless marble showers, and freestanding tubs for Miami Shores homes, with prewar plumbing realities handled honestly and every project permitted through the Village and inspected at each stage.
intro_paragraphs: Most Miami Shores houses were generous about everything except bathrooms. A 1920s Mediterranean Revival near NE 96th Street might have one original bath serving four bedrooms, and the ranches near the Country Club settled for a hall bath and a sliver of a master. The bathroom remodeling owners here actually want is a primary suite: two rooms combined, a marble shower you can stand in with your elbows out, a freestanding tub, and storage that ends the hallway-closet shuffle. That conversion is most of our bath work in the Village.

Bathroom remodels are permitted through the Miami Shores Village Building Department, with plumbing, electrical, and inspections in sequence along the way. Prewar houses here often carry their original cast-iron drain stacks and galvanized supply lines, so we scope the plumbing honestly before you commit, because replacing pipe during the remodel costs far less than opening finished marble later. Purely interior work stays out of design review, but a new or enlarged window brings in the Village's harmony standards and an impact-rated, Miami-Dade approved unit. We work both sides of that line every week.

Waterproofing is the part of a bathroom nobody photographs, so it is the part we supervise hardest: membranes carried to the right height, pans flood-tested before tile, slopes checked before stone goes down. PGX Builders Group is a licensed general contractor, CGC1539072, and every bath we build is permitted and inspected, no exceptions. You get a fixed scope in writing, finish materials protected from the first day of demolition, and one team accountable from estimate through warranty.

faqs.q: Do bathroom remodels in Miami Shores need permits and inspections?
faqs.a: Yes. Plumbing, electrical, and the build itself are permitted through the Miami Shores Village Building Department and inspected in sequence. Waterproofing is the step that deserves the most scrutiny, and we flood-test shower pans before tile regardless of what the minimum requires. Every bathroom we build in the Village is fully permitted; it protects your resale, your insurance, and frankly our license.

faqs.q: What surprises hide in a 1920s bathroom remodel?
faqs.a: Cast-iron drain stacks near the end of their life, galvanized supply lines closing up from the inside, framing that was never square, and tile set in thick mortar beds that come out by the wheelbarrow. None of it is exotic. We have opened enough prewar walls in the Shores to price the likely findings up front and put contingencies in writing instead of springing them on you mid-project.

faqs.q: Can you turn two small rooms into a primary suite?
faqs.a: That is the most requested bathroom project in Miami Shores' older homes: borrow a small bedroom or an oversized closet, and the floor plan finally yields a real suite with double vanity, frameless shower, freestanding tub, and actual storage. It involves structural review, new plumbing runs, and permits, all of which we handle. The result usually changes how the whole house lives, not just the morning routine.

faqs.q: Does a new bathroom window need Village approval?
faqs.a: Changing the exterior for light or ventilation engages Miami Shores Village's harmony standards and requires an impact-rated window carrying a Miami-Dade product approval. Purely interior remodels stay out of design review entirely. We tell you which side of that line your project sits on during the first walk-through, so review time is in the schedule from day one rather than discovered in week six.

faqs.q: How much does a high-end bathroom remodel run?
faqs.a: A primary suite with stone, custom glass, and relocated plumbing is a substantial five-figure project at minimum and often beyond, depending on how far the layout moves. We position ourselves honestly: not the cheap bid, but the fixed-scope one, with waterproofing done to our standard, materials protected, and inspections passed. You will know the real number before demolition because it will be in writing.

home-additions.title: Miami Shores Home Additions & Second Stories | PGX Builders
home-additions.meta_description: Home additions in Miami Shores: rear extensions and second stories designed to match the original house and clear Village review. Call (786) 273-2524.
home-additions.h1: Additions that pass the harmony test
home-additions.hero_sub: Rear extensions, second stories, and garage conversions across Miami Shores, engineered for older masonry houses, permitted through the Village, matched to the original architecture, and supervised daily from footings to final.
home-additions.local_heading: Additions that match the original architecture
intro_paragraphs: Families in Miami Shores tend to stay: the schools, the Country Club, the ten-minute geometry of the Village. That is why home additions are such a strong market here. Owners of 1920s Mediterranean Revival homes near Grand Concourse and the bayfront streets add rear wings and second stories rather than trade away their architecture, while ranch owners west of Biscayne Boulevard add family rooms and primary suites. The brief is always the same: make it look like the house was always this size.

Additions run through the Miami Shores Village Building Department, and the Village's code holds exterior work, additions and renovations included, to a harmony standard, with the Planning and Zoning Board reviewing what does not fit its surroundings. Setbacks and lot coverage shape what the site will carry. On bayfront streets like North Bayshore Drive, FEMA enters the math: parts of the shoreline sit in VE flood zones, and substantial-improvement rules can determine how far a renovation goes before elevation requirements apply. We model that before you fall in love with a floor plan.

An addition is structural work on a house you are still living in, which is why PGX assigns daily supervision from the first footing to the final inspection. We handle the tie-beam and foundation engineering older masonry homes need to carry new loads, match barrel tile and stucco texture so the seam disappears, and keep the occupied side of the house sealed, clean, and functioning. Fixed written scope, a licensed general contractor, CGC1539072, and one accountable team through every inspection.

faqs.q: Will my addition go before the Planning and Zoning Board?
faqs.a: Possibly. Miami Shores Village holds exterior work, additions included, to a harmony standard covering character and appearance, and projects that do not clearly meet it are reviewed by the Planning and Zoning Board, which meets monthly. Designing to the standard from the start, with massing, materials, and rooflines that agree with the original house, is how we keep review from turning into redesign.

faqs.q: Can a 1920s Miami Shores house carry a second story?
faqs.a: Many can, but nobody should promise it before the engineering. We evaluate the existing foundations and masonry; the answer is often yes with tie-beam upgrades and reinforcement, and occasionally no at reasonable cost. Where a second story pencils, it doubles usable space without touching the yard. Where it does not, a rear extension usually gets you there. We give you the structural answer before you commit to a direction.

faqs.q: Do FEMA flood rules affect additions near the bay?
faqs.a: On bayfront and canal-adjacent properties, yes. Parts of the Miami Shores shoreline along Biscayne Bay sit in VE flood zones, and FEMA's substantial-improvement rules compare your project's value against the building's; cross the threshold and elevation requirements can apply to more than just the addition. That math should shape the design early, so we run it during planning rather than after permitting stalls.

faqs.q: How long does a home addition take in Miami Shores?
faqs.a: Realistically, months of design and permitting before months of construction. Additions involve structural plans, multiple plan reviews, and possibly board review, and building through South Florida's rainy season takes sequencing discipline. We give you a schedule tied to your specific scope at contract, and daily supervision is how it stays honest. Anyone quoting a fast, precise timeline before drawings exist is guessing.

faqs.q: Is an addition worth it versus moving?
faqs.a: In Miami Shores, often yes. The housing stock is finite, the character is why you came, and a well-built addition adds space without giving up your street. That said, we will tell you when a project does not pencil: if the structure, the setbacks, or the flood math fight the plan, better to know at the walk-through than at permit review. We would rather lose a project than build a bad one.

outdoor-living.title: Outdoor Living & Exterior Work in Miami Shores | PGX Builders
outdoor-living.meta_description: Outdoor living in Miami Shores: terraces, summer kitchens, and exterior work built for salt air, HVHZ wind loads, and Village color rules. Call (786) 273-2524.
outdoor-living.hero_sub: Terraces, summer kitchens, pergolas, and full exterior renovations for Miami Shores homes: permitted, engineered for the High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, and built by a licensed contractor who supervises the details daily.
intro_paragraphs: Miami Shores lives outdoors most of the year, with bay breezes off Bayfront Park, golf light over the Country Club, and dinner on the terrace in January. The high-end outdoor living work here follows that rhythm: covered terraces off 1920s Mediterranean Revival homes, summer kitchens built for actual cooking, pergolas shading a pool deck, and driveways and stucco brought up to the standard of the rest of the house. Done well, the yard becomes the best room the house has.

Exterior work is precisely where Miami Shores Village pays attention. The code requires buildings to stay harmonious with their neighborhood in character, appearance, and exterior color, and nonstandard colors need advance approval from the Planning and Zoning Board. Every structure you add must meet High-Velocity Hurricane Zone wind loads with Miami-Dade approved products, permitted through the Village Building Department. Near the bay and the Biscayne Canal, king tides belong in the drainage plan and salt air belongs in the material selection. We design for the review and the weather at the same time.

PGX Builders Group runs exterior projects as one coordinated scope instead of five trades guessing at each other's schedules: the gas line goes in before the stone counter, the roof tie-ins happen before the paint, the driveway gets poured after the heavy equipment leaves. Licensed, insured, permitted, and inspected, CGC1539072, with a written scope and a supervisor who shows up daily. Twenty-plus years in South Florida taught us that exteriors fail at the details, so the details get supervised.

faqs.q: Do I need approval to change my exterior paint color in Miami Shores?
faqs.a: For nonstandard colors, yes. The Village code requires advance Planning and Zoning Board approval for nonstandard colors and multicolored roofs, and exteriors generally must stay harmonious with the neighborhood. It is one of the quirks that keeps the Shores looking like the Shores. When repainting is part of a larger exterior project, we fold the color question into the same approval path as everything else.

faqs.q: Can you build a summer kitchen at my house?
faqs.a: Yes, and a real one, not a grill on pavers. A proper summer kitchen involves gas or dedicated electrical, plumbing if you want a sink, ventilation under a covered roof, and counters in materials that handle salt air. Each trade is permitted and inspected through the Village. We design it around how you actually cook outside, then build it to survive both hurricanes and Thanksgiving.

faqs.q: Do pergolas and terraces really need hurricane engineering?
faqs.a: In Miami-Dade's High-Velocity Hurricane Zone, yes. Anything with a roof or sail area is designed to wind loads, anchored accordingly, and built with approved products; that is what keeps a pergola a shade structure instead of a projectile. It is also what plan review will require regardless. Engineering an outdoor structure properly costs little compared to rebuilding it, or a neighbor's fence, after a storm.

faqs.q: What about drainage and king tides near the bay?
faqs.a: East of Biscayne Boulevard and along the Biscayne Canal, water is part of the design brief. King tides raise the baseline a few times a year, so hardscape elevations, drainage paths, and material choices are planned to stand up to occasional saltwater rather than pretend it will not happen. It rarely changes what you can build; it changes how we detail and pitch it.

faqs.q: How do you price outdoor projects?
faqs.a: As one coordinated scope with a fixed written price: terrace, summer kitchen, hardscape, and any roof or stucco work sequenced by one team instead of five overlapping subcontractors. High-end exterior work is unforgiving of shortcuts, so we do not take them, and we do not bury games in allowances. Walk the yard with us and you will get a real number tied to a real plan.
